items.definition: A set of rooms for living in on one floor of a larger building. In American English it is called an apartment.
examples: We share a two-bedroom flat near the station.

items.definition: A part of a town or city where people live, especially when you think about the people and atmosphere there.
examples: It's a friendly neighbourhood with a market and plenty of small cafés.

items.definition: An area on the edge of a large town or city where there are mostly houses, often rather quiet and comfortable.
examples: They moved to a leafy suburb so the children could have a garden.

trap.en: In Spanish, suburbio often suggests a poor, rough area. In British English a suburb is usually a pleasant residential area, and it is not a negative word.
trap.es: Suburb no tiene el matiz de «barrio pobre» que tiene «suburbio». Suele ser una zona residencial tranquila a las afueras.

items.definition: A person who owns a house or flat and lets it to other people in return for rent.
examples: Our landlord has promised to repair the heating before winter.

items.definition: A person who pays rent to live in a house or flat that belongs to someone else.
examples: The tenants complained about the damp in the bathroom.

items.definition: The path at the side of a road where people walk. In American English it is called a sidewalk.
examples: Please don't cycle on the pavement; it's dangerous for pedestrians.

items.definition: The part of the day when roads and public transport are busiest because people are travelling to or from work.
examples: Avoid the underground during the rush hour if you can.

items.definition: A long line of vehicles that cannot move, or can only move very slowly.
examples: We got stuck in a traffic jam for an hour on the way into town.
collocations: be stuck in a traffic jam

items.definition: The money you pay for a journey on a bus, train, taxi or other form of public transport.
examples: Bus fares have gone up again this year.
The taxi fare from the airport was higher than I expected.

items.definition: Used for people's homes rather than for shops, offices or factories.
examples: The council wants to keep traffic out of residential streets.

items.definition: In bad condition because no one has looked after it or spent money on it.
examples: The town centre looked run-down after most of the shops had closed.

items.definition: Becoming popular and successful, or likely to do so soon.
examples: Young artists are moving into this up-and-coming part of the city.

items.definition: A very tall building divided into many flats or offices.
examples: They live on the twelfth floor of a tower block with views over the river.

items.definition: A large group of houses or flats built together in the same area, usually planned at the same time.
examples: She grew up on a housing estate on the edge of Sheffield.

items.definition: A main road that goes around a town or city so that traffic does not have to pass through the centre.
examples: Take the ring road if you want to avoid the town centre.
collocations: the ring road around the city
